text:
maya: quick note — ran a 6h perf sweep on stage after the KV-cache eviction change. prefill latency p95 jumped ~27% for long context (6k-12k).
liam: ouch. is this only prefill or decode too?
sasha: mostly prefill. decode steady or slightly better. looks like batching got worse once prefill and decode started mixing in the same queue.
maya: exactly — the continuous-batcher was merging prefill (large per-request cost) with decode (many short bursts). we got token budget blowouts and kernel selection started to pick fallback kernels.
andre: repro was a producer of long prompts + streaming. devbench summary: p50 unchanged, p95 prefill 27% up, p99 up 40%. CPU upwards during prefill windows.
cory: quick diff points to commit abc1234: changed queue_budget accounting to global token budget instead of phase-aware. that means prefill requests could consume decode tokens.
liam: i pushed a small local tweak: split queues + phase-aware token caps. config snippet:
```
batching:
  split_prefill_decode: true
  token_budget_per_phase:
    prefill: 1536
    decode: 512
  queue_policy: phase_aware_priority
  prefill_batch_target_tokens: 4096
  decode_batch_max_latency_ms: 10
```

liam: with that, prefill batching forms larger but sparser batches; decode keeps small low-latency batches.
sasha: did you also force kernel selection to prefer fp16-attn when prefill tokens > 1024?
liam: yes, added a kernel_hint override for large prefill sequences. fall back still allowed.
maya: ran benchmark after tweak: p95 prefill back within 5% of baseline, p99 within 8%. decode p95 improved slightly thanks to lower queue contamination.
andre: interesting KV-cache behavior: prefill-heavy batches were thrashing KV cache because the runtime tried to merge KV slices across batches. we now pin KV pages per prefill batch and evict only on low-memory pressure. that cut page-in churn by ~60%.
cory: perf regression root cause = combined effect: (1) global token accounting introduced cross-phase noise, (2) kernel fallback due to merged batch shape, (3) KV page churn from aggressive KV coalescing.
maya: next steps: (a) land split-queue + phase caps behind feature flag, (b) add telemetry for "batch_phase_mix" metric (counts mixed-phase batches), (c) add devbench CI check for mixed-phase-induced kernel fallbacks.
liam: i've got a patch ready, running canary on staging now. will flip flag for 2 small customers tomorrow.
ops-bot: deploy/ci — staging canary for batcher-split started at 2024-10-18T22:14:00Z :rocket:
devbench-bot: perf-run summary 1742101300: prefill_p95 1.05x baseline, decode_p95 0.98x baseline, kv_page_in_rate -62%
sasha: nice. once canary stable we should also tune token budgets per-model type (chat vs completion). large-chat needs higher prefill caps.
maya: agreed. i'll write up a short runbook for oncall: how to toggle feature flag, thresholds to revert, and quick checks (mixed-phase metric, kernel-fallback-rate, kv_page_in_rate).
andre: can we autoscale prefill workers instead of increasing latency for decode? autoscale + phase_cooldown could be cheaper.
liam: noted — autoscale policy draft in PR.
maya: thanks team — this is a good win. followups in the eng-runtime sprint board. :tada:
